part_legend.B: Forecast-start state-initialization procedure -- generic recipe; only t0 itself moves per experiment

decisions.value: elif ((qw >= deficit) and ait((qw + w_q) <= ...)) -> elif (qw >= deficit) and ((qw + w_q) <= ...):
decisions.evidence: Fixed in BOTH scripts/vendor/snow17.py and scripts/vendor/snow17_instrumented.py. Exercised successfully across all 694 Sierra cells in the smoke test and across the full Stage-1 production calibration/held-out pipeline with no errors.
decisions.notes: If you vendor a fresh copy of tonic Snow-17, check for and fix this bug -- do not assume an upstream download is already patched.

decisions.evidence: model_swe = w_i + w_q, read directly from vendored source
decisions.notes: SWE alone is NOT the complete state -- two snowpacks with identical SWE can have different deficit/w_q/ait and melt differently going forward.

decisions.value: No restart-state API exists in either vendored copy. snow17() hardcodes all 5 states to 0.0 internally at call start and only returns model_swe/outflow arrays for the whole input series -- it does not accept an initial-state argument and does not return final state. snow17_instrumented.py additionally RETURNS the 5 state trajectories but still does not ACCEPT them as input.
decisions.evidence: Direct inspection of scripts/vendor/snow17.py lines 116-126 (zero-init) and function return statement (only model_swe, outflow); scripts/vendor/snow17_instrumented.py lines ~43-47 (also zero-init) and its return statement (adds trajectories but still no state-input parameter).
decisions.notes: Consequence: continuation across a forecast start date requires ONE continuous snow17() call spanning spin-up + forecast (Option B), never state serialization (Option A) -- Option A is not currently implementable without modifying the vendored function, which has not been done in this repo. This is the answer to 'can Snow-17 state be serialized/restarted': no, not with the current implementation.

decisions.value: dt (Snow-17 integration timestep) != forecast lead time. dt must match the actual cadence of the time/prec/tair arrays passed in; snow17() asserts equal shapes and does not resample.
decisions.evidence: DT_HOURS = 24 confirmed by direct grep across scripts/stage1_calibrate.py, scripts/snow17_smoke_test_wy1985.py, scripts/spinup_experiment.py -- the current baseline uses daily forcing, dt=24, not 6-hourly.
decisions.notes: Explicitly flagged, not silently reconciled, against docs/intern/permultter_snow17.md's 6-hourly forcing discussion -- that document's section describes a different, Phase-2/ACE2-oriented procedure, not this project's current daily-timestep observational baseline. ACE2's own native cadence is 6-hourly (see ace2_precipitation_conversion decision); an experiment using ACE2 forcing can and should run Snow-17 at dt=6 directly rather than forcing resampling to daily.

decisions.value: Held-out whole-Sierra: daily NSE=0.934, RMSE=65.4mm, r=0.982 (WY2005-2020); April-1 NSE=0.931, r=0.991, sign/anomaly agreement=93.75% across 16 years. Adding WY2021: daily NSE=0.934, April-1 r=0.991 (essentially unchanged).

Melt-timing lag (mean |peak-date error| 17-22 days) in dry years. Do not use the frozen theta uncritically for drought-year-specific analysis without reading the full report.

decisions.value: occupancy-weighted regional mean: SWE_r(t) = sum_i(w_ir * SWE_i(t)) / sum_i(w_ir), w_ir = native region-r pixel count per ERA5-Land cell. Whole-Sierra extends the same formula with W_r = total occupancy weight per region.
decisions.evidence: Implemented in scripts/snow17_smoke_test_wy1985.py (inline) and scripts/stage1_pipeline_common.py (reusable function, preferred for new work); w_ir sums cross-checked self-consistent
decisions.notes: Naive equal-weighted mean-of-cell-means produced -28.6% to -32.6% low bias vs native flat mean, WY2021 check. Prefer stage1_pipeline_common.py's reusable implementation over re-copying the smoke test's inline version for new work.

decisions.value: dz = z_target_terrain - z_(elevation represented by the forcing). The forcing-referenced elevation is NOT automatically ERA5-Land's orography -- it must be determined per forcing source before reusing the formula.
decisions.status: NEW, derived 2026-09-11 to prevent a different forcing source's temperature being substituted while keeping z_ERA5Land fixed
decisions.evidence: Generalization of the elevation_correction decision's Sierra-specific instantiation; cross-checked against docs/ACE2_Snow17_Scientific_Validity_Rule.md's independent requirement for a documented elevation-correction manifest per production run
decisions.notes: ERA5-Land forcing -> use ERA5-Land orography (current baseline). ACE2 -> determine elevation represented by ACE2's own grid (HGTsfc field) before reusing the formula -- not yet done/verified in this repo. Another model -> determine its forcing-grid reference orography first.

decisions.value: T_corrected = T_ERA5Land + (-4.5 K/km) * (z_DEM - z_ERA5Land) / 1000
decisions.status: RESOLVED, PRODUCTION (applied throughout Stage-1 forcing cache)
decisions.evidence: Sign convention verified against Dutra Eq.1; elevation mismatch audit quantified Delta z; applied in scripts/stage1_cache_forcing.py
decisions.notes: This is the ERA5-Land-specific INSTANTIATION of elevation_correction_generic_rule -- z_ERA5Land is only the correct reference term when your forcing source is actually ERA5-Land. Full Sierra mean dz=+263.3m median=+216.9m; South mean=+359.8m; ge_1000m fraction Full Sierra=1.30%, South=5.08% (verified exactly from elevation_stats.json; an earlier recalled ~5.6% figure does not exactly match either and is flagged, not reconciled).

decisions.evidence: Dutra et al. (2020) own observationally-derived optimal constant (clrO) for western US incl. Sierra; outperforms -6.5 K/km; not significantly beaten by variable daily/monthly ELR, especially for land-surface snow depth/soil temperature
decisions.literature_reference: Dutra, E. et al. (2020). Environmental Lapse Rate for High-Resolution Land Surface Downscaling: An Application to ERA5. Earth and Space Science, 7(3). DOI:10.1029/2019EA000984
decisions.notes: Exact Dutra model-level method infeasible locally (no ERA5 model-level archive). Pressure-level approximation explicitly rejected: only 1-3 of Dutra's 9 native 500-1200m-AGL levels available at representative Sierra cells, worst at highest elevations. PDF filename uses a Unicode hyphen (U+2010) in 'High-Resolution' -- copy-paste the exact filename rather than retyping.
